findings.title: Failed work items are marked complete and their offsets are committed
findings.body: OrderedQueueWorker.run catches every exception from result_processor, logs it, and then unconditionally calls offset_tracker.complete_offset in the finally block. The commit loop can therefore advance past a message that was never successfully processed, contradicting the strategy's documented 'only commits after successful processing' guarantee and causing permanent data loss on transient processing failures instead of redelivery.

findings.title: Unbounded queues provide no backpressure and can grow without limit
findings.body: FixedQueuePool creates queue.Queue() with no maxsize, and SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.submit always returns immediately after put(). Despite the docstring claiming natural backpressure, the Arroyo consumer will keep polling Kafka and enqueueing messages as fast as it can fetch them even if workers are stuck or slow, leading to unbounded in-memory growth/OOM and a huge backlog of fetched-but-uncommitted offsets.

findings.title: Strategy close/terminate discards queued work by shutting down the shared pool
findings.body: SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.close() sets the commit shutdown event and immediately calls queue_pool.shutdown() without first waiting for queues to drain (wait_until_empty is never used). FixedQueuePool.shutdown sets worker.shutdown=True, so a worker exits at the top of its loop after its current item even if its queue still holds items. On Arroyo partition revocation/rebalance this abandons in-flight messages, and because the same pool is shared (see result_consumer factory), closing one strategy instance also kills the pool for any subsequently created strategy: queue.put then raises queue.ShutDown, which submit()'s catch-all converts into add+complete offset, silently committing unprocessed messages.

findings.title: Catch-all in submit marks offsets complete for messages never enqueued
findings.body: submit() wraps decoding, grouping and queue submission in one try/except and, on any exception, adds and immediately completes the offset. This conflates poison messages with transient failures: e.g. grouping_fn raising, queue shutdown raising queue.ShutDown, or the real decode_payload asserting on FilteredPayload (decode_payload asserts payload is not FilteredPayload) all cause the offset to become committable even though nothing was processed, silently dropping the message with only a log line.

findings.title: Kafka offsets are committed from a background thread
findings.body: _commit_loop runs in its own thread and calls commit_function (the Arroyo Commit callable supplied to create_with_partitions) from there. Arroyo processing strategies are driven single-threaded by StreamProcessor and the commit callable/consumer commit path is not documented as thread-safe; invoking it concurrently with the main consumer loop risks races with the processor's own ONCE_PER_SECOND commit logic and with partition assignment changes, potentially committing offsets for partitions no longer owned.

findings.title: Group-to-queue assignment uses Python's randomized hash()
findings.body: get_queue_for_group uses built-in hash(group_key) % num_queues. For str keys hash() is randomized per process via PYTHONHASHSEED, so the 'consistent hashing' claimed in the docstring is not stable across restarts or across consumer processes: the same subscription is assigned to a different queue whenever the process restarts, breaking the ordering/affinity guarantee the pool exists to provide relative to any other process or previous incarnation. A stable digest (e.g. md5/sha like other Sentry grouping code) is required.

findings.title: Committable-offset scan is O(offset range) every second per partition
findings.body: get_committable_offsets iterates range(start, max_offset+1) and is invoked every second by the commit loop. When one slow item blocks a partition (the exact scenario this PR targets), the outstanding window grows with throughput, so each scan walks an ever-larger range of integers doing two set lookups per offset, and all_offsets keeps every uncommitted offset in memory. A single stuck subscription can thus make commit processing progressively more expensive and delay commits for all partitions.

findings.title: Queue pool and offset tracker are never reset on partition reassignment
findings.body: The FixedQueuePool (and its OffsetTracker) is created once in the factory __init__ and reused for every create_with_partitions call. OffsetTracker state (all_offsets, outstanding, last_committed) is keyed only by Partition and is never cleared when partitions are revoked or reassigned, and last_committed starts at -1 regardless of the committed position Arroyo passes in the partitions mapping. After a rebalance, stale outstanding entries from the previous assignment can permanently block commits for a reassigned partition, or stale last_committed state can cause incorrect committable calculations for a partition this consumer no longer owns or newly owns at a different position.
